label: churn100-s7
summary: The model predicts telecom churn from three main routes, added on the logit scale. First, heavy daytime use without a voice mail plan: a usage score built from day minutes and charge (plus evening and night minutes) acts on 1364 of the 2939 training customers without a voice mail plan and on 0 of the 1061 with one, and a second step makes risk climb steeply for the heaviest users. Second, customer service calls: a gate opens once calls pass a small threshold for customers whose usage score is off (for the typical customer predicted risk goes from 1.8% to 25.0% across it), but the usage score shuts it, so heavy users need many more calls. Third, an international plan adds a step that takes the typical customer from 1.8% to 24.7%. A voice mail plan unit, offsets for a few states and small linear terms (international calls down, international charge up) adjust the score. Removing the usage pathway lowers training AUC from 0.919 to 0.655. The South Dakota terms look fitted to 66 customers.
